candidates.title: Fish first
candidates.body:
Got every fish across the water. Put my feet down for the grass. They stopped before the rest of me did.

Lay on my chest with my bill held up. Kept the fish clean. Picked grass out of my own feathers later.

candidates.title: One more turn
candidates.body:
Put my feet down for the landing. A gust lifted me and I went round again.

On the next pass I tucked them up. The grass was still there. Everything was going so well while I wasn't touching it.

preservedUnillustratedProse.title: Width problem
preservedUnillustratedProse.literalBody: Flew home with fish sticking out of both sides of my beak. Reached the burrow. Turned my head sideways to fit. The fish fitted beautifully. My head was now sideways in a hole.

preservedUnillustratedProse.title: The final pebble
preservedUnillustratedProse.literalBody: A clean flight, a gentle landing, three steady steps. Then the little pebble outside my door rolled under my foot and I sat down in the grass. I have crossed the sea more easily than this pebble.
preservedUnillustratedProse.status: unillustrated draft, not a spent admitted event; preserved unchanged

preservedUnillustratedProse.title: The last six feet
preservedUnillustratedProse.literalBody:
The wind carried me over the swell all morning. I rose through it, turned, and fell back toward the water without once needing to hurry. A bird far below became a white fleck behind me.

At the headland I spread my feet and came down beside the grass. One foot touched. The other found a hollow. My wings, which had been so useful over an entire ocean, now filled every available direction.

I stopped with my beak in a plant. A beetle was climbing its stem. It carried on past my eye. I stayed there until it had gone, then pulled myself upright as though I had come specifically to examine it.
